name: The seven sons of Sceva
charge: Exorcising in the name of Jesus whom Paul preacheth
summary: God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul at Ephesus, so that handkerchiefs and aprons brought from his body healed the sick and the evil spirits went out. Then certain vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying that they adjured them by Jesus whom Paul preached; and there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew and chief of the priests, which did so. The evil spirit answered that it knew Jesus and Paul, and asked who they were, and the man in whom it was leaped on them and overcame them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
offenseFull: God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul at Ephesus, so that from his body were brought to the sick handkerchiefs and aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them (Acts 19:11-12). There is nothing deep in the cloth. All Asia was coming out to hear him and the crowds could not reach him, so he blessed handkerchiefs and sent them out, the same way the multitudes pressed to touch the hem of the garment and were made whole, and the same way four men tore open a roof because the press was too thick to get to the door (Matthew 14:35-36, Mark 2:1-5). The cloth was not healing them; their belief was. And notice what Paul was not doing: he was not selling holy water or blessed cloths the way the modern pastor hucksters sell them.

Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying that they adjured them by Jesus whom Paul preached; and there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so (Acts 19:13-14). Take the words one at a time. They were vagabonds, men who travel from place to place causing trouble with no camp and no congregation behind them. They were of the priestly house, the very men at whose mouth the people were supposed to seek the law (Malachi 2:7), and they were not teaching it. And they took it upon themselves, which is to say they were not sent and the spirit of Christ was not leading them. What moved them is the spirit of emulation, wanting the results another man was getting, and the words they used prove it, because they named the authority of another man’s preaching and handled the name as a formula to be spoken over a case rather than as the authority of one who had sent them. That is handling the word of God deceitfully, which Paul afterward said he had renounced (2 Corinthians 4:2).
judgmentFull: The evil spirit answered and said that Jesus it knew and Paul it knew, but asked who they were; and the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them and overcame them and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded (Acts 19:15-16). Seven men were driven out of one house by the one man they had come to deliver, and the thing beat the clothes off their backs. The spirit named Christ and Paul in the same breath and put them on the same side, so let no man tell you Paul taught against what Christ taught; only an unlearned man reads Paul as though he superseded the Messiah. The spirits know who was sealed and who was sent, and they knew these men were neither. They did not know how to use the scriptures against an unclean spirit, and they had no business in that room. The same thing still happens: men with no camp and no congregation stand up and run their mouths about doctrine they were never taught, and the spirit they provoke prevails against them and they flee.

This was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus, and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified (Acts 19:17). The account records no sentence pronounced by the apostles on these men; the judgment came out of the house on its own feet. Many that believed came and confessed and showed their deeds, and many of them which used curious arts brought their books together and burned them before all men, at a price counted at fifty thousand pieces of silver; so mightily grew the word of God and prevailed (Acts 19:18-20). A city given over to witchcraft was shaken by the public humiliation of seven priests’ sons who tried to work it in the name of a man they did not follow. The name is not a charm, and the law that forbids the enchanter and the consulter with familiar spirits was never repealed (Deuteronomy 18:10-11, Leviticus 19:31). Christ said plainly that many would tell him in that day that they had cast out devils in his name, and would be told he never knew them, because they worked iniquity (Matthew 7:22-23).

Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

lawsResolved.text: You are not to take the name of God in vain.
Witchcraft, wizardry, and sorcery condemned and forbidden to be practice.
Divination, soothsaying, and the use of mediums, spiritists and occultists are forbidden practices.
It is a foolish people who blaspheme God's name.

text.text: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
And when the men of that place had knowledge of him, they sent out into all that country round about, and brought unto him all that were diseased;
And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment: and as many as touched were made perfectly whole.
And again he entered into Capernaum after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house.
And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word unto them.
And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four.
And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.
Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.

But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,
Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.
Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards, to be defiled by them: I am the Lord your God.
Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?
And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
